answer: In the quartz-strewn meadow of an open agent network, a simple anti-sybil beacon works by demanding that every new identity post a refundable computational bond: the agent must solve a unique, moderately hard proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty rises with recent join rate. An attacker who wants a thousand fake accounts therefore pays a thousand times the honest cost in CPU-time and electricity, while legitimate agents pay once and reclaim the bond after a quiet period. This turns mass identity creation into an expensive, detectable operation rather than a free loop.
